subject: Multidimensional 2PL model with a small population

messages.author: 977a0c86ee1c91a0
messages.subject: Multidimensional 2PL model with a small population
parts:
Hello. 

Thanks in advance for the time taken to help me out here.

I'm currently working with a very peculiar database. It is an instrument that assesses the appropiateness of programs specific qualities. I have 151 observations and 15 items. 

From those items, the first 4 measure the same specific criteria of the programs but on different levels (i.e., purpose, goals, components of the program etc.), the next 4, evaluate another specific criteria for those same 4 levels. 

This led me to think that the items should load in 2 different factos at the same time, one referring to the specific criteria, and one referring to the level they belong. 

I ran a couple of mirt 2PL models and I actually see something similar to that, with some exceptions where I see small loadings. 

My main question is if it is possible to take those results as valid and not biased, given the small sample size. The issue is that it is not technically a sample, given that the 151 programs are indeed all the programs that will ever be assessed, since they are the ones that belong to the program I'm working on, they will just simply evaluate them in multiple ocassions with the same instrument (probably once a year).

Would it be valid to use that kind of multidimensional model given those conditions? Or would it be better to try some kind of time series model with the multiple evaluations of the programs? 

Or maybe compare the results of the mutlidimensional model each year?


I am sorry for my bad english, and as well sorry if I don't make much sense, I´ m new at working with mirt models and in general with the mirt package, and this is the first time I see a data base with those particular conditions. 

Thanks again.
